title: Per-corpus Dynamic INT8 Calibration + Cosine Watchdog for Embedding Stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a repeatable calibration and validation pipeline that produces per-corpus INT8 scale/zero-point profiles for embedding models and a lightweight cosine-similarity drift watchdog. Targets: reduce median embedding storage/throughput cost by using INT8 with FP16 fallback for edge cases, and detect semantic drift within 24h for high-traffic customers. The feature includes: (1) automated bucketed calibration that groups tokens/activation ranges by corpus and sequence-length distribution, (2) a validation harness that computes cosine similarity distributions between FP16 baseline and INT8-quantized outputs across labeled test sets, stratified by domain, and (3) a production monitor (cosine watchdog) that raises alerts when percentile shifts exceed configurable thresholds and triggers automatic fallback to FP16 variants for affected routes.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline can ingest corpora (S3/Drive) and produce per-corpus INT8 profiles with metadata (quantile histograms, bucket boundaries) within 2 hours for corpora up to 500k examples

Validation harness computes cosine similarity (mean, median, 1/5/95 percentiles) between FP16 baseline and INT8 outputs and reports regression flags when median similarity drops below 0.98 or 5th-percentile drops below 0.92
Cosine watchdog metric emitted to Datadog/Grafana with percentiles and daily drift score; alert policy documented and tested with simulated drift
Router integration can switch a route to FP16 fallback for >1% of requests when composite regression score exceeds policy, and fallback is reversible via rollout control

Runbook and automated tests exist: unit tests for quant profile generator, integration tests for validation harness using synthetic drift datasets, and an end-to-end canary demonstrating rollback behavior
implementation_steps: Design quantization profile schema: bucketed scales, per-layer activation ranges, corpus_id, sample_stats; finalize spec with storage format (parquet) and versioning scheme
Implement calibration worker: sample selection, per-bucket min/max and quantile estimator, outlier clipping policy, produce profile artifact and checksum
Build validation harness: take FP16 model outputs as baseline, run INT8-inference simulation using profile, compute cosine similarity metrics and aggregated histograms
Create synthetic drift generator for QA: token shuffling, adversarial paraphrase injection, and domain-shift sampler to exercise percentile regressions
Expose metrics: percentiles p50/p05/p95, drift_score, quant_profile_applied, fallback_rate; wire to Datadog and create dashboard
Router & runtime integration: policy engine to evaluate drift_score per-corpus or per-route, and automated switch logic to FP16 variants with rate limits
Canary rollout: instrument 1% of traffic for early customers, run for 72h, collect metrics and postmortem checklist
Documentation: runbook, API for submitting corpora and requesting new calibration runs, and guidance for PMs/solutions engineers
notes: Why per-corpus? We observed that single global calibration often masks domain-specific tails causing 5th-percentile similarity regressions in niche datasets.
Bucketed calibration reduces quantization bias for long-tail activation ranges while keeping profile size small compared to per-layer full histograms.
Trade-offs: more profiles = higher storage and lookup overhead; we limit to one profile per customer-domain and fallback heuristics when unknown corpus_id seen.
Fallback strategy: immediate FP16 fallback on sustained regression, with a decayed retry policy for reapplying INT8 profile after re-calibration
Security: profiles contain only aggregate statistics, no raw text; confirm with Security for customers requiring additional audit trail (flag added if requested)
